Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=1+ti+(t2−5)j+(3t−1)k at the point P(2,4,8), valid for all real values of u?

a
2i+4j+8k+u(14i−6j−3k)
b
2i+4j+8k+u(14i+3j−3k)
c
2i+4j+8k+u(14i+6j+3k)
d
2i+4j+8k+u(i+6j+6k)
e
2i+4j+8k+u(i+6j+3k)
Submit

decision.explanation: At P, 3t−1=8 gives t=3, and r(3)=(2,4,8). Differentiating gives r'(t)=(1/(2√(1+t)),2t,3), so r'(3)=(1/4,6,3). The tangent line is P+u r'(3) for every real u, matching option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve  $r(t)=\sqrt{1+t}\,i+({t}^{2}-5)\,j+(3t-1)\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8),$  valid for all real values of $u?$
after.worked_solution:
The point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
R(u)=r({t}_{0})+u\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

where ${t}_{0}$ corresponds to the value of $t$ at the point $P.$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ \sqrt{1+t}\,i+({t}^{2}-5)\,j+(3t-1)\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+t}=2 \\ {t}^{2}-5=4 \\ 3t-1=8\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the third equation, we get $t=3.$ This value also satifies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(3).$  

We calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{1+t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1)\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+t}}\,i+2t\,j+3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+(3)}}\,i+2(3)\,j+3\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}\,i+2\cdot 3\,j+3\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,i+6\,j+3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point $P(2,4,8)$ is

$$
R(u)=2i+4\,j+8\,k+u(\frac{1}{4}\,i+6\,j+3\,k),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 1

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=1+ti+(t2−5)j+(3t−1)k at the point P(2,4,8), valid for all real values of u?

a
2i+4j+8k+u(14i−6j−3k)
b
2i+4j+8k+u(14i+3j−3k)
c
2i+4j+8k+u(14i+6j+3k)
d
2i+4j+8k+u(i+6j+6k)
e
2i+4j+8k+u(i+6j+3k)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The point P(2,4,8) is at the tip of r(t) for some specific value t0 of the parameter t. At this point the vector r′(t0) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as

R(u)=r(t0)+ur′(t0),u∈(−∞,∞),

where t0 corresponds to the value of t at the point P.

First, we find the value of t that corresponds to P. We know that:

r(t)=2i+4j+8k1+ti+(t2−5)j+(3t−1)k=2i+4j+8k,

and equating the coefficients of i,j, and k yields the following system:

{1+t=2t2−5=43t−1=8

From the third equation, we get t=3. This value also satifies the other two equations. Therefore, P(2,4,8) is at the tip of the vector r(3).

We calculate r′(t):
r′(t)=ddt(1+t)i+ddt(t2−5)j+ddt(3t−1)k=121+ti+2tj+3k

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=3:

r′(3)=121+(3)i+2(3)j+3k=124i+2⋅3j+3k=14i+6j+3k

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point P(2,4,8) is
R(u)=2i+4j+8k+u(14i+6j+3k),u∈(−∞,∞).

content.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve  $r(t)=\sqrt{1+t}\,i+({t}^{2}-5)\,j+(3t-1)\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8),$  valid for all real values of $u?$
content.worked_solution:
The point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
R(u)=r({t}_{0})+u\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

where ${t}_{0}$ corresponds to the value of $t$ at the point $P.$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ \sqrt{1+t}\,i+({t}^{2}-5)\,j+(3t-1)\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+t}=2 \\ {t}^{2}-5=4 \\ 3t-1=8\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the third equation, we get $t=3.$ This value also satifies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(3).$  

We calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{1+t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1)\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+t}}\,i+2t\,j+3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+(3)}}\,i+2(3)\,j+3\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}\,i+2\cdot 3\,j+3\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,i+6\,j+3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point $P(2,4,8)$ is

$$
R(u)=2i+4\,j+8\,k+u(\frac{1}{4}\,i+6\,j+3\,k),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨1−4t2,5t+1⟩ at the point where t=−1, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨2,9⟩
b
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩
c
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨−3,4⟩
d
⟨1,−2⟩+u⟨8,5⟩
e
⟨1,−2⟩+u⟨−3,4⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: At t=-1, r(-1)=⟨-3,-4⟩. Since r'(t)=⟨-8t,5⟩, r'(-1)=⟨8,5⟩. Thus the tangent line is ⟨-3,-4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩ for all real u, matching option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨1-4{t}^{2},5t+1⟩$ at the point where $t=-1,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
after.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=-1,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(-1)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(-1)+u{r}^{′}(-1),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨1-4(-1)^{2},5(-1)+1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-8t,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(-1) & =⟨-8(-1),5⟩ \\  & =⟨8,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=-1$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨-3,-4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨1−4t2,5t+1⟩ at the point where t=−1, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨2,9⟩
b
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩
c
⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨−3,4⟩
d
⟨1,−2⟩+u⟨8,5⟩
e
⟨1,−2⟩+u⟨−3,4⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

At the point where t=−1, the vector r′(−1) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as R(u)=r(−1)+ur′(−1),u∈(−∞,∞)

First, we find r(−1): r(−1)=⟨1−4(−1)2,5(−1)+1⟩=⟨−3,−4⟩

Now, we calculate r′(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(1−4t2),ddt(5t+1)⟩=⟨−8t,5⟩

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=−1: r′(−1)=⟨−8(−1),5⟩=⟨8,5⟩

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where t=−1 is
R(u)=⟨−3,−4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩,u∈(−∞,∞).

content.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨1-4{t}^{2},5t+1⟩$ at the point where $t=-1,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
content.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=-1,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(-1)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(-1)+u{r}^{′}(-1),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨1-4(-1)^{2},5(-1)+1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-8t,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(-1) & =⟨-8(-1),5⟩ \\  & =⟨8,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=-1$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨-3,-4⟩+u⟨8,5⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

decision.explanation: The tangent vector is r'(t)=⟨3t+4,6t+9⟩. Parallelism to ⟨1,3⟩ requires 6t+9=3(3t+4), giving t=-1. Then r'(-1)=⟨1,3⟩ and r(-1)=(-5/2,-6), so option a is correct.

Question 5

Given the curve r(t)=1ti+(t2−3)j, t∈(0,∞), find all points at which r′(t) and r(t) are parallel.

a
 (2,−114)
b
(1,−2)
c
 (12,1) and (1,−2)
d
(2,−114) and (12,1)
e
 (12,1)
Submit

decision.explanation: r'(t)=⟨-1/t²,2t⟩. Parallelism requires the determinant (1/t)(2t)−(t²−3)(-1/t²)=3−3/t² to equal zero. Thus t²=1, and since t>0, t=1 only. The point is r(1)=(1,-2), matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j,$ $t\in (0,\infty ),$ find all points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-3)\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ \frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j & =c(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}i+2t\,j) \\ \frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j & =-\frac{c}{{t}^{2}}i+2ct\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $i$ and $j$ gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t}=-\frac{c}{{t}^{2}} \\ {t}^{2}-3=2ct\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation we obtain $-t=c.$ Substituting $c=-t$ into the second equality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-3 & =-2{t}^{2} \\ 3{t}^{2}-3 & =0 \\ 3(t+1)(t-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =\frac{1}{1}\,i+({1}^{2}-3)\,j \\  & =\,i-2\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(1,-2).$

content.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j,$ $t\in (0,\infty ),$ find all points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-3)\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ \frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j & =c(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}i+2t\,j) \\ \frac{1}{t}\,i+({t}^{2}-3)\,j & =-\frac{c}{{t}^{2}}i+2ct\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $i$ and $j$ gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t}=-\frac{c}{{t}^{2}} \\ {t}^{2}-3=2ct\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation we obtain $-t=c.$ Substituting $c=-t$ into the second equality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-3 & =-2{t}^{2} \\ 3{t}^{2}-3 & =0 \\ 3(t+1)(t-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =\frac{1}{1}\,i+({1}^{2}-3)\,j \\  & =\,i-2\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(1,-2).$
